thread.title: Google sold at least $2.7 billion worth of hardware during the holidays

title: Google sold at least $2.7 billion worth of hardware during the holidays
text:
Alphabet Inc.-owned Google pocketed about $2.7 billion from hardware sales during the fourth quarter, according to MarketWatch calculations.
Buried in the company’s financial results largely revolving around the search giant’s $27.23 billion advertising business lies revenue known as Google Other, which banked $4.69 billion in the fourth quarter. Of that, Alphabet Chief Financial Officer Ruth Porat said Google’s cloud division made $1 billion , which is the first time in years the company has disclosed its revenue.
Revenue in Google Other came from hardware—which includes the company’s Pixel smartphone and Home speaker sales—cloud and Play Store, in order of greatest to least, a spokeswoman said. If the cloud unit is in the middle, Play Store must be making $1 billion or less.
That leaves hardware with the remainder of the Google Other segment: about $2.7 billion.
Don’t miss: ‘Google is at Apple’s mercy’ — the trouble in Alphabet’s earnings 
While it’s potentially slightly more, depending on Play Store revenue, or less, if there are additional businesses Google is not disclosing within Other (and Play Store drove far less revenue), it’s likely in the ballpark.
While cloud was the largest contributor in the third quarter, and remains a fast-growing segment, Google’s new lineup of hardware, announced in October , likely made a significant contribution to that $2.7 billion number — especially with the seasonal boost from holiday sales. Among the new gadgets on sale for the holiday quarter that Google launched: its new Pixel 2 smartphones, a virtual-reality accessory for the phones, wireless ear buds, as well as a range of new smart speakers. The most inexpensive speaker, the Google Home Mini—aggressively marketed and priced at a discount for much of the holiday season at $30—was the easiest way for consumers to access the company’s virtual assistant.
Jackdaw Research analyst Jan Dawson has told MarketWatch that he expects the Home Mini to be Google’s mass-market product. “It’s one of the only ones that may show up in financial results,” he said.
While the new products aren’t flawless — a bug on the Mini forced the company to make changes — and reviews not always perfect , $2.7 billion in quarterly sales is nothing to sneeze at. But it’s still dwarfed by rival Apple Inc. AAPL, -3.59% and its $61 billion in quarterly iPhone revenue, or 77.3 million units , not to mention its other hardware.
At the moment, analysts polled by FactSet model $4.09 billion in first-quarter sales and $5.83 billion in this year’s December quarter for the Other unit.
Alphabet stock GOOGL, -5.16% GOOG, -4.45% fell about 5% in Friday trading. The class A stock has gained 45% in the past 12 months, with the S&P 500 index SPX, -1.74% rising 24%.
This article has been updated to clarify that hardware sales figures were not disclosed directly by Alphabet.
